title: field-voices-compact-sprint-briefing
content:
Executive summary:

Quick read: this compact briefing synthesizes 34 customer threads (support, CSM calls, partner calls) from Apr–May 2026 into three prioritized friction clusters and a small bucket of low-effort probes we can execute in a single sprint. Goal is fast signal -> small rollback-safe changes that reduce observed latency tail events and improve perceived cost controls for mid-market customers.

Why this doc: many long-form CS rundowns exist; this one is intentionally minimal, biasing for action: top themes, 6 candidate fixes ranked by expected impact/time-to-ship, and clear next owners.

Top-level themes (summary):
- Theme A — Tail latency and cold-start variability: customers report spiky 95th/99th percentile latency on hosted endpoints during bursty workloads, especially for chat sessions with long histories. Triggered often after inactive periods.
- Theme B — Cost unpredictability for multi-turn chat and reranking: token billing feels opaque when caching/batching changes behavior; customers want clearer levers and quick cost-estimates for feature flags (e.g., prefix caching on/off).
- Theme C — Model variant fallbacks and degradations: when higher-tier models hit capacity, automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants yields unpredictable quality drops; customers request more visible downgrade annotations and optional stricter rollbacks.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "Our 99th p95 jumped to 3.2s during a 10-min burst — users noticed. We need a predictable tail, not just averages." — B2B support app
- "We love the caching but can’t explain cost spikes when we enable it for some flows. Is it batching or long-context expansion?" — fintech analytics startup
- "Fallback to the quantized v2 without an option to pin to the older smaller model cost us 12% conversion. We need better safety nets." — marketplace product team

Priority map (impact vs effort, short notes):
1) Probe: Explicit cold-start hedging (low-effort) — HIGH impact / LOW effort. Implement a thin warmup ping path and optional warmup-on-deploy flag per-tenant. Expect measurable reduction in 95th latency for idle-to-burst cases. 1–2 engineer days to wire through gateway + metrics.
2) Feature: Cost-preview API for route configs (medium-effort) — HIGH impact / MED effort. Add a best-effort cost estimator endpoint that simulates typical token usage given prompt templates and routing policies. Roughly 1 sprint (frontend + backend + small UX).
3) Probe: Transparent fallback annotations in response headers (very low-effort) — MED impact / VERY LOW effort. Surface model-variant and quantization metadata in responses (x-model-variant, x-fallback-reason). 1 engineer day.
4) Improvement: Burst-aware autoscaler smoothing (med-effort) — MED-HIGH impact / MED effort. Modify autoscaler to use short-term smoothing window for sudden burst detection instead of instantaneous scale-downs. 1–2 sprints with SRE + infra review.
5) Feature: Per-tenant caching controls in Console (med-effort) — MED impact / MED effort. Allow toggling prefix/KV caching per route with estimated cost delta. Requires UI, API and apply logic.
6) Investigation: Reranker billing audit (low-effort investigation) — UNKNOWN impact / LOW effort. Quick audit of token accounting for reranking flows; reconcile with a top 10 customer invoice discrepancy list. 2–3 days of billing + infra logs work.

Estimated engineering costs (T-shirt sizes):
- #1 Warmup ping: XS (0.25–0.5 engineer-weeks)
- #2 Cost-preview API: M (1–2 engineer-weeks across backend + product design)
- #3 Response header annotations: XS (0.1–0.25 engineer-weeks)
- #4 Autoscaler smoothing: L (2–4 engineer-weeks incl testing & rollout plan)
- #5 Console caching controls: M (1–3 engineer-weeks incl UX + QA)
- #6 Reranker billing audit: S (0.5–1 engineer-weeks, billing + infra)

Suggested quick probes for next 2 sprints (concrete):
- Probe A (Sprint 1): Deploy warmup pings for a subset of tenants (5 pilot customers). Metric: 95th latency drops; target 20% reduction for idle-to-burst within 7 days. Rollback plan: disable warmup if cost delta > 5% or no latency improvement. Owner: eng-infrastructure (Omar S.).
- Probe B (Sprint 1): Add x-fallback-reason header on a canary host. Expose to 3 internal customers for feedback. Metric: number of support tickets referencing unexpected fallbacks. Owner: serving-runtime (Ben R.).
- Probe C (Sprint 2): Launch cost-preview MVP in console for one route type (text-generation). Metric: usage of preview feature and correlation with route toggles enabling caching. Owner: product-hosted-api (Aisha P.).

Open questions & risks (notes to self):
- Warmup pings could increase cost for infrequent customers; need billing guardrails. Which customers are OK with this being on by default?
- Cost-preview accuracy ceiling: we'll present a range (low/median/high) not a guarantee. How do we communicate uncertainty in UI?
- Fallback annotation could increase security/ops surface (don’t leak internal model names). Use safe-coded labels.

Customer segments most affected:
- Mid-market SaaS (20–200 engs) with heavy multi-turn chat
- Fintech analytics (sensitive to latency tails)
- Marketplace teams with sensitive conversion metrics and strict quality SLAs

Suggested rollforward plan (lightweight):
- Week 0: Align triage with SRE + Billing + Product. Confirm pilot customers and feature gating. (Owner: Aisha P.)
- Week 1: Ship Probe A and Probe B as canaries. Monitor metrics daily; report snapshot at EOW. (Owners: Omar S., Ben R.)
- Week 2: Iterate on telemetry and quick fixes. Start Cost-preview UX wireframe. (Owners: product-hosted-api + design)
- Week 3–4: Expand pilots based on results, prepare rollout runbook with opt-out flag and billing fallback.

Acceptance criteria for probes:
- Warmup ping: 95th latency improvement >= 15% on pilot cohort without >4% cost increase
- Fallback header: Provide meaningful signal in >=80% of fallback events; none should expose internal variants
- Cost-preview: Customers report that estimates are directionally useful in >60% of trials

Linked tickets / suggested JIRA tasks:
- CS-4321: Pilot warmup ping for hosted API
- CS-4322: Add fallback metadata headers and limit exposure
- CS-4323: Console cost-preview wireframe -> MVP
- CS-4324: Reranker billing audit (billing team)

Misc notes (stream-of-consciousness style):
- Several customers suggested a toggle: "Prefer quality over cost when fallback occurs" — could be a per-route preference with default = cost-balanced.
- UX: show an inline "why this dial matters" tooltip when toggling caching (small copy needed).
- Consider light A/B of warmup ping: ping vs no-ping randomization for same tenant subsets to measure causal effect.

Next steps (immediate):
- [ ] Triage meeting Wed 2026-05-19 10:00 PT (invite SRE, Billing, Product, Serving). Owner: Aisha P.
- [ ] Create the 4 JIRA tasks (owner: Ben R.) by EOD 2026-05-20
- [ ] Confirm pilot customer list (CS outreach): Clara N. to produce list by 2026-05-21

End note: this is intentionally pragmatic — prioritize experiments that lower customer pain quickly even if they are conservative. Keep feedback loop tight (48–72h) and log all customer reactions into CS-4321 thread for traceability.

Unresolved items to capture in the triage:
- What default settings should we recommend for newborn tenants?
- Billing guardrails thresholds for warmup pings
- Internal naming convention for header annotations (security constraint)

Comments welcome — ping me or drop edits inline.
